skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure that CloudWatch Log Group is encrypted by KMS

check_result.suppress_comment: AWS-owned encryption (CloudWatch Logs' default) is sufficient for execution/detection logs containing no secrets or PII — a customer-managed CMK costs ~$1/month/key for no meaningful benefit at this project's scale. See SECURITY.md.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure CloudWatch log groups retains logs for at least 1 year

check_result.suppress_comment: 14-day retention (var.log_retention_days) is a deliberate cost control, not an oversight — see COST.md. This is a personal lab with no compliance requirement to retain execution logs for a year.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure that AWS Lambda function is configured for a Dead Letter Queue(DLQ)

check_result.suppress_comment: No DLQ configured — a reasonable v2 enhancement (see SECURITY.md's Known Limitations), deliberately out of scope for this project's size. EventBridge itself retries failed async Lambda invocations before giving up.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure that AWS Lambda function is configured inside a VPC

check_result.suppress_comment: Deliberately NOT in a VPC — this function only calls AWS service APIs (SNS, IAM, Lambda) and needs neither internet egress nor access to any VPC-private resource. VPC placement would require NAT Gateway (~$32/month, against this project's cost philosophy) or VPC endpoints for no security benefit against this threat model. See SECURITY.md.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure AWS Lambda function is configured to validate code-signing

check_result.suppress_comment: Code-signing (AWS Signer) is a software-supply-chain control disproportionate to a personal portfolio lab — noted as a future enhancement in SECURITY.md, not implemented here.

skipped_checks.check_name: Check encryption settings for Lambda environmental variable

check_result.suppress_comment: Environment variables here (SNS_TOPIC_ARN, RESPONDER_FUNCTION_NAME, LAB_USER_ARN) are resource identifiers, not secrets — confirmed by code review. Lambda already encrypts them at rest with an AWS-owned key by default; a customer CMK adds cost/complexity for no benefit to non-sensitive values.

skipped_checks.check_name: X-Ray tracing is enabled for Lambda

check_result.suppress_comment: X-Ray tracing not enabled — a reasonable observability enhancement, deliberately deferred (see SECURITY.md's Known Limitations) to keep this project's scope focused on detection/response rather than broader AWS feature coverage.

check_result.suppress_comment: Same reasoning as aws_lambda_function.detector above.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure access is controlled through SSO and not AWS IAM defined users

check_result.suppress_comment: This IS the finding, not a gap. A directly-defined IAM user with a direct policy attachment (instead of SSO / group membership) is exactly the over-permissioned legacy identity pattern this entire project exists to detect and contain — see this file's header comment and IAM_DESIGN.md. Checkov flagging it here confirms the scanner works correctly, the same way tests/offline/test_checkov_scan.py's known-bad fixture does deliberately.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure IAM policies are attached only to groups or roles (Reducing access management complexity may in-turn reduce opportunity for a principal to inadvertently receive or retain excessive privileges.)

check_result.suppress_comment: Same reasoning as aws_iam_user.lab above — a policy attached directly to a user (rather than a group/role) is the deliberate subject of this project, not an oversight.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure CloudTrail defines an SNS Topic

check_result.suppress_comment: CloudTrail's native SNS notification (one message per delivered log file) is a legacy/alternative pattern this project deliberately does not use — detection is driven entirely through EventBridge's native CloudTrail integration instead (see terraform/modules/detection/main.tf), which was chosen during this project's design phase specifically because it's free for same-account delivery, unlike the CloudWatch Logs subscription alternative. Enabling this too would be redundant, not a fix.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs

check_result.suppress_comment: SSE-S3 (AES-256) on the destination bucket already encrypts the log objects at rest. A customer-managed KMS key for the trail itself costs ~$1/month for no meaningful benefit to a personal lab's non-regulated data — see the identical trade-off noted on aws_s3_bucket.trail above and in COST.md.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure the S3 bucket has access logging enabled

check_result.suppress_comment: Access logging would require a SECOND bucket to receive access logs about the trail bucket itself — cost/complexity disproportionate to a personal lab. The trail already captures management-event API calls made against this bucket (PutBucketPolicy, PutBucketAcl, etc. — see detections/D-02-logging-tamper.md); what's not captured is object-level data-plane access (GetObject/PutObject), which this project's threat model does not need visibility into.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure S3 buckets should have event notifications enabled

check_result.suppress_comment: This project deliberately routes detection through EventBridge's native CloudTrail integration (see terraform/modules/detection/main.tf), not S3 event notifications on this bucket — a different, already-documented notification mechanism, not a gap. S3 event notifications would fire on "a new log object appeared," which isn't the signal this project's detections evaluate.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs

check_result.suppress_comment: Deliberately not integrated with CloudWatch Logs — that delivery path costs $0.50/GB at this project's low-volume scale (AWS's ingestion pricing is tiered; verified during this project's design phase) and EventBridge's native CloudTrail integration is free for the same-account use case this project needs. See ARCHITECTURE.md/COST.md for the original cost comparison this decision was based on.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure that S3 bucket has cross-region replication enabled

check_result.suppress_comment: Cross-region replication is a disaster-recovery control, not a security one, and adds a second bucket's worth of ongoing cost — disproportionate to a $5/month personal lab budget. See COST.md.

skipped_checks.check_name: Ensure that S3 buckets are encrypted with KMS by default

check_result.suppress_comment: SSE-S3 (AES-256, set below) already encrypts all data at rest. A customer-managed KMS key costs ~$1/month for no meaningful benefit to a personal lab's non-regulated log data — the same trade-off already called out in this file's own SSE comment below and in COST.md.
